metadata.title: CESNET-CC25: Dataset for detection of C&C communication of botnets in the IP flow format
metadata.description:
CESNET-CC25 is a dataset of real-world botnet Command-and-Control (C&C) communication and benign traffic from an Internet service provider backbone, created to evaluate the detection of modern botnets in network traffic, including decentralized architectures and encrypted communication. It contains 32 captures of live botnet samples of the families Mirai, Gafgyt, Hailbot, Kaiji, Miori and Xorbot, 1,380 hours of C&C traffic (160,743 IP flows) and 194 million benign IP flows from the CESNET3 network. Existing datasets such as CTU-13 are more than a decade old and mostly short; CESNET-CC25 captures contemporary threats over long periods (up to 167 hours per sample), which is essential for multi-flow and periodicity-based detection.

The CESNET-CC25 dataset in three formats

  • PCAP (raw botnet packets): https://zenodo.org/records/16752462
  • IP flows (ipfixprobe, CSV): https://zenodo.org/records/16753890 (this record)
  • Periodic features of multiflow time series (CSV): https://zenodo.org/records/16753981

This record holds the dataset as IP flows in CSV, exported by ipfixprobe: the botnet flows extracted from the PCAP captures and the benign flows of the CESNET3 network (anonymized IP addresses). Besides the usual flow fields, the records include packet-level sequences (packet lengths, directions and inter-packet times) for detailed per-flow analysis.

How the data were captured

  • Botnet traffic was captured in an isolated laboratory: each botnet binary ran in its own virtual machine on a bare-metal host, the traffic was mirrored at the router and recorded with tcpdump on a dedicated monitoring probe. The traffic was supervised continuously and every malicious activity other than the C&C communication (e.g. attack traffic) was promptly identified and blocked.
  • Benign traffic comes from live traffic of CESNET3, the Czech national research and education network, exported as IP flows by ipfixprobe on monitoring probes behind network TAPs. The IP addresses of the benign traffic were anonymized.

Directory structure

  • benign/: benign IP flows from the CESNET3 network
  • botnet/<folder>/: IP flows of one botnet sample (table below)

Recommendations for use

  • Build detectors on the statistical and behavioural features; leave out identifiers such as IP addresses, port numbers and protocol types. They are short-lived and do not generalize across networks and time.
  • Botnet and benign traffic were captured at different points of the infrastructure, so inter-packet timing may differ for technical reasons; using it directly as a classification feature risks overfitting.
  • Single flows of the two classes often look alike: the 160,743 botnet flows contain only 2,458 unique packet-length and direction sequences and part of them also occur in benign traffic. Multi-flow approaches (e.g. the periodic features record) avoid this ambiguity.

Safety notice

The data contain real malicious traffic and the addresses of real C&C servers that were active at the time of capture. Use them for research and defence only; do not connect to the listed servers. The botnet binaries themselves are not part of the dataset.
